interest: Shows Japanese insurers repatriating $5.5 million pre-freeze, with State and NY regulators declining to intervene before formal controls.
overview: This file (894.5062) contains U.S. Department of State correspondence and internal memoranda from October through December 1940 concerning the voluntary liquidation and withdrawal from the United States of two Japanese marine insurance companies operating in New York. Louis H. Pink, Superintendent of Insurance of the State of New York, approached Herbert Feis, Adviser on International Economic Affairs, reporting that the companies planned to transfer their business to an American insurer and remit surplus reserves of approximately $5.5 million back to Japan after securing creditor obligations. The State Department, noting that no existing law or regulation controlled or restricted such capital transfers, officially declined to comment or object to the New York Insurance Department and forwarded copies to the Treasury Department. Internal routing slips and notes document subsequent review and circulation of the issue among senior officials, including Stanley K. Hornbeck, Henry F. Grady, and Sumner Welles.

subfiles.about: Account of a conference with New York Insurance Commissioner Louis H. Pink regarding the liquidation of two Japanese insurance companies and the repatriation of $5.5 million to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Pink tells Feis two Japanese insurers in New York will cease operations, transferring business to an American insurer while keeping reserves for creditors and sending $5.5 million surplus back to Japan; Feis finds no law restricting the transfer and will check for further instructions.
